summary: Over a 14-day evaluation period, closed-loop automated insulin delivery via AAPS achieved an 86.0% Time in Range with a mean glucose of 121.6 mg/dL. Time below range is 5.1%, exceeding the standard 4% safety threshold, driven primarily by early overnight lows (00:00-02:00 local). Postprandial elevations occur in afternoon hours (13:00-18:00 local) due to unannounced meals and delayed gastric emptying associated with GLP-1 therapy.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM data integrity and telemetry completeness are exceptionally high with 98.7% coverage over 14 days and 3,995 valid entries.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid entries, 10 minor gaps with largest gap 65 minutes, 2,315 treatments, and 6,214 device statuses.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Total absence of explicit carbohydrate entries (0g total) as management relies entirely on UAM and automation.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall glycemic control is strong, but time below range of 5.1% requires attention, particularly during early sleep hours.
analysis_steps.evidence: Mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, SD 39.7 mg/dL, CV 32.6%, TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%, with glucose extremes dipping to 42 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of explicit meal carb entries limits direct evaluation of postprandial insulin matching.

analysis_steps.findings: Early overnight hours (00:00-02:00 local) show increased time below range (up to 18.5% at 01:00 local), indicating that the 0.6 U/h basal rate and 90 mg/dL target may be slightly aggressive during early sleep.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local hourly glucose averages show 90.6-93.3 mg/dL between 00:00 and 01:00 local with elevated TBR; stable 99-106 mg/dL from 03:00 onwards.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact sleep onset and evening meal tail-end effects cannot be fully separated without carb logs.

analysis_steps.findings: The flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U is conservative for daytime corrections, but Oref1 dynamic sensitivity (70% factor) and SMBs actively scale real-time delivery.
analysis_steps.evidence: Profile ISF is 56 mg/dL/U flat; CR ranges from 10.5 to 13.2 g/U; DIA is 10 hours. Correction windows show variable efficacy against afternoon peaks.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of explicit carb entries prevents direct validation of CR segments.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled and operating correctly, providing vital automated coverage for unannounced meals given the lack of manual carb entry.
Autosens is disabled while Dynamic ISF is active at 70%, successfully compensating for the static profile ISF during high-demand windows.

analysis_steps.findings: The user relies on unannounced meal management via UAM/SMB and Dynamic ISF, combined with GLP-1 therapy (1.25mg) which delays gastric absorption and causes afternoon plateau highs.
analysis_steps.evidence: Zero carb entries in treatment summary; therapy response windows show correction responses; GLP-1 logs on Aug 14, 17, and 20.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of precise meal timing and size documentation.

analysis_steps.findings: Carbohydrate absorption relies entirely on UAM detection with min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min and a 7-hour max absorption window, appropriately supporting GLP-1 delayed kinetics.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic control is strong overall, but early overnight hypoglycemia (5.1% TBR) and afternoon postprandial rises require staged verification before modifying insulin delivery settings.
analysis_steps.evidence: Complete synthesis of data quality, safety overview, basal segments, automation settings, and meal strategy.

recommendations.title: Monitor Early Overnight Basal and Target
recommendations.description: Time below range reaches 5.1%, with early overnight hours (00:00-02:00 local) showing up to 18.5% below range. Verify whether early sleep low readings are driven by residual evening insulin action or basal rate 0.6 U/h before making profile adjustments.

recommendations.title: Evaluate Meal Logging for Afternoon Peaks
recommendations.description: Afternoon glucose levels show elevated time above range (up to 32% between 15:00-16:00 local) due to unannounced meals interacting with GLP-1 delayed absorption. Consider logging meal times and approximate carb amounts to improve automated UAM response.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Current profile settings supported by Oref1 dynamic sensitivity and UAM automation maintain an 86% Time in Range. While early overnight hypoglycemia (5.1% TBR) is present, changes should be withheld until further observation of overnight IOB and evening meal clearance.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor early overnight glucose (00:00-02:00 local) for 5 consecutive days to verify if low readings persist before considering a minor basal reduction at 00:00.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings unchanged while monitoring early overnight glucose and evaluating meal logging.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Management relies entirely on unannounced meal detection (UAM), automated micro-boluses (SMBs), and Dynamic ISF (70%) to handle unannounced meals and GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying.

exceptions.pattern: Afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia peaks (13:00-18:00 local) due to unannounced absorption outpacing UAM response.
exceptions.suggestion: Introduce manual meal announcements or pre-meal micro-boluses for known carbohydrate intake.
exceptions.rationale: Mitigates afternoon time above range without increasing hypoglycemia risk.

exceptions.pattern: Early overnight hypoglycemia (00:00-02:00 local) reaching up to 18.5% time below range.
exceptions.suggestion: Verify that evening correction activity and UAM SMBs have fully cleared prior to sleep.
exceptions.rationale: Reduces overall time below range footprint from 5.1% toward the <4% target.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain closed-loop UAM and SMB automation with a 3-minute interval, active Dynamic ISF (70%), and a 7-hour max absorption window, supplemented by optional manual meal announcements for known carbohydrate loads to smooth afternoon postprandial plateaus.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log precise meal times and approximate carbohydrate grams for 3 to 5 days to evaluate postprandial glucose trajectories and refine meal strategy.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Continue monitoring CGM metrics, focusing specifically on early overnight glucose (00:00-02:00 local) and time below range.
Step 2: Observe afternoon postprandial glucose patterns (13:00-18:00 local) to determine if unannounced meal logging improves peak control.
Step 3: Review active IOB clearance before sleep to ensure early overnight hypoglycemia risk is minimized.
Step 4: Consult care team independently before making any changes to basal rates or profile settings.
education: Closed-loop systems using UAM (Unannounced Meal) rely on rapid detection of rising glucose to deliver automated micro-boluses, but delayed gastric emptying from GLP-1 therapy can flatten and extend postprandial absorption peaks.
Time below range above 4% indicates potential over-delivery or residual insulin stacking during sensitive windows like early sleep.
